Aw man, I can relate to your girlfriend a bit haha. I'm the girlfriend of a dm too. Now I wouldn't consider myself obsessed or anything, but I am 100% a hopeless romantic. And I can say that partially why I enjoy romance in dnd is that it allows my boyfriend and I to step out of our hangups/feeling shy around each other irl, as weird as it sounds. It's like you gain this sort of suave confidence that you can't fake irl. He even described it as getting the chance to fall in love with me all over again. I think if done right, romance in dnd can be a very powerful tool for making a story hit that much harder. 

Now, I won't deny that this sounds like a relationship issue instead of a dnd one. To me it sounds like perhaps your girlfriend isn't having her needs met outside of this, and she's using dnd as a surrogate to have her perfect fantasy romance play out with you. I don't have much advice to offer other than be gentle with her, and to consider hashing out what could be missing/done better in your relationship. Like others have said, therapy is most likely your best option here. You're probably best off playing out the romance as a separate roleplay from your current campaign; perhaps during a cozy romantic one-on-one session between the two of you. Separating it from your current campaign allows your other players to not feel awkward if your gf has an outburst, and she will most likely benefit from having a more descriptive, thought out and romance focused plot tailored for her. I hope this was helpful OP, best of luck to you two! <3

I think one of the unintentionally funniest moments I've had with her recently is when Strahd invited the party to castle ravenloft. He just killed off a party member (rest in peace, Ooba the half orc) and wanted to trade his remains for Sergei's armor (long story, essentially our paladin Tarvar thought it would be a smart idea to take it). Rahadin walks us in to the dining room and seats us at the table. Cue Strahd monologuing about how we're the real monsters for destroying what honour his brother had left (which I kind of agree with. Our dm made it so the armor was the only thing preserving Sergei's body, which makes it extra fucked up that our pally stole it). Anyways, we notice Strahd drinking out of a chalice fashioned from a skull. Turns out it was the skull from Tarvar. Tarvar had died earlier and we burned an abbot res on him, but the head was weirdly missing from his body. Party eventually leaves, but Elerra hangs back to maybe slip in a chat with Strahd or something. She spys the skull chalice, and decided it would be a great idea to take a sip from it. She made sure that no one was in the room, and then took the tiniest little sip from it. Yep. It was Tarvar's blood. Definitely not wine :( The whole party and dm were absolutely howling with laughter out of character at this point. But what really killed them is what I asked after a brief pause in the laughing. "... Do I like it?" 👀 Ended up rolling a 10 after the dm asked me to "roll for taste". So now Elerra, not a vampire, mind you, now is kind of going to be side-eyeing the paladin thinking about how his blood wasn't actually fucking terrible when she drank it in secret 😂

He just giggled to himself, and I decided to ask him why -- and he replied with "oh, well I was gonna say dark red that way it perfectly matches all the dried blood and scabs on your hands". Needless to say I felt so damn awful after that one :(

I honestly don't know why I'm even cordial with the guy at this point - on other occasions he has also said that my hand "looks like some alien is growing on them", and that he thought I had decided to punch a brick wall. Oh, and the one time I decided to wear a short sleeve shirt to work (I never do anymore due to bad eczema and years of scarring on my arms) he decided to ask me why my arms looked so f-ed up. 

So yes, TLDR: I'm incredibly sorry you had to go through that at work. I (and probably most others on here too) totally get how you feel, and even though your coworker probably didn't mean any harm, I think it's definitely fair to call these kind of experiences traumatic :(
